valuation.method: Forward Non-GAAP EPS x P/E (FY2027 Non-GAAP diluted EPS viewed at the 12-month target date)

bear.driver: AI data center power deployment delays or grid-interconnection normalization compress revenue growth and gross margin expansion

base.driver: Continued hyperscaler and commercial on-site fuel cell scaling toward ~$7.0B FY2027 revenue with sustained ~34% gross margins

bull.driver: Accelerated multi-gigawatt framework conversions (Oracle, NTT DATA, Brookfield) drive operating leverage above consensus

valuation.implied_by_close: At base FY2027 Non-GAAP EPS of $5.25, the $191.99 close implies 36.6x forward P/E; at 42.0x, the close implies $4.57 EPS.
valuation.sensitivity: One turn of P/E moves the base target by $5.25 (+2.7 pp at the $191.99 close).
valuation.watch_metric: Product revenue growth, Non-GAAP gross margin (~34.5% in Q3 2026), and multi-gigawatt data center backlog conversions

analyst_notes: Following Bloom Energy's Q3 2026 beat and third full-year guidance raise on October 22, 2026 (FY2026 revenue raised to $4.4B-$4.6B, Non-GAAP EPS to $3.10-$3.40), named analysts largely maintained or upgraded to Buy/Overweight/Outperform ratings while recalibrating targets amid November AI-infrastructure volatility. Barclays and BMO Capital Markets upgraded to Overweight and Outperform in November even while trimming targets to $289 and $230, respectively, whereas Morgan Stanley ($335) and RBC Capital ($335) sit well above our $220.50 base case. The Street's higher targets reflect willingness to underwrite ~55x-64x our $5.25 base FY2027 EPS or higher 2027 earnings power.
